25107-sarre-o-1901.description: A book by Louis Becke. oke on that cruise in the _Fanny Lang_, by a boat being stove in by a whale. So after I had got my money I walked out of the office, thinking of going to Sydney by the steamboat, when up comes Sarréo.

arxiv-2106-01447.title: A generalisation of the Poincaré-Hopf Theorem.
arxiv-2106-01447.creator: Aaron Pim
arxiv-2106-01447.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Aaron Pim. The Poincaré-Hopf Theorem is a conservation law for real-analytic vector fields, which are tangential to a closed surface (such as a torus or a sphere). The theorem also governs real-analytic vector fields, which are tangential to surfaces with smooth boundaries; in these cases, the vector field must be pointing in the outward normal direction along the boundary [ 6 , 2 ] .

arxiv-2306-08231.description: Abstract Université Paris Cité École Doctorale de Sciences Mathématiques de Paris Centres (ED 386) Instituet de Mathématiques de Jussieu-Paris Rive Gauche (UMR 7586) présenté par Xiaofa CHEN THÈSE DE DOCTORAT DE MATHÉMATIQUES Dirigée par Bernhard KELLER Présentée et soutenue publiquement le 11 Juillet 2023 devant le jury composé de: \displaystyle\textbf{Mme Claire AMIOT} \displaystyle\text{MCU-HDR} \displaystyle\text{Universit\'{e} Grenoble Alpes} \displaystyle\text{Examinatrice} \displaystyle\textbf{M Xiao-Wu CHEN}

arxiv-2306-13770.title: Meta-Path-based Probabilistic Soft Logic for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction CCS: Applied computing Bioinformatics CCS: Information systems Association rules CCS: Mathematics of computing Markov networks CCS: Theory of computation Convex optimization
arxiv-2306-13770.creator: Shengming Zhang, Yizhou Sun
arxiv-2306-13770.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Shengming Zhang, Yizhou Sun. Drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction, which aims at predicting whether a drug will be bounded to a target, have received wide attention recently, with the goal to automate and accelerate the costly process of drug design. Most of the recently proposed methods use single drug-drug similarity and target-target similarity information for DTI prediction, which are unable to take advantage of the abundant information regarding various types of similarities between them.

arxiv-2312-15771.title: Simultaneous Optimal System and Controller Design for Multibody Systems with Joint Friction using Direct Sensitivities
arxiv-2312-15771.creator: Adwait Verulkar 1, Corina Sandu 1, Adrian Sandu 2, Daniel Dopico 3
arxiv-2312-15771.description: Abstract Real-world multibody systems are often subject to phenomena like friction, joint clearances, and external events. These phenomena can significantly impact the optimal design of the system and its controller. This work addresses the gradient-based optimization methodology for multibody dynamic systems with joint friction using a direct sensitivity approach for gradient computation.

arxiv-2412-00543.title: Evaluating the Consistency of LLM Evaluators
arxiv-2412-00543.creator: Noah Lee, Jiwoo Hong, James Thorne
arxiv-2412-00543.description: Abstract Large language models (LLMs) have shown potential as general evaluators along with the evident benefits of speed and cost. While their correlation against human annotators has been widely studied, consistency as evaluators is still understudied, raising concerns about the reliability of LLM evaluators.

arxiv-2412-05852.title: Evolving Algebraic Multigrid Methods Using Grammar-Guided Genetic Programming Thanks: Presented at the Copper Mountain Conference on Iterative Methods, April 2024.
arxiv-2412-05852.creator: Dinesh Parthasarathy
arxiv-2412-05852.description: Abstract Multigrid methods despite being known to be asymptotically optimal algorithms, depend on the careful selection of their individual components for efficiency. Also, they are mostly restricted to standard cycle types like V-, F-, and W-cycles. We use grammar rules to generate arbitrary-shaped cycles, wherein the smoothers and their relaxation weights are chosen independently at each step within the cycle.

arxiv-2501-16790.title: Exponential Family Attention
arxiv-2501-16790.creator: Kevin Christian Wibisono
arxiv-2501-16790.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Kevin Christian Wibisono. The self-attention mechanism is the backbone of the transformer neural network underlying most large language models. It can capture complex word patterns and long-range dependencies in natural language. This paper introduces exponential family attention (EFA) , a probabilistic generative model that extends self-attention to handle high-dimensional sequence, spatial, or spatial-temporal data of mixed data types, including both discrete and continuous observations.

arxiv-2503-09222.title: Energy Conditions and Stability of Charged Wormholes in f ⁡ ( R , ℒ m ) f(R,\mathscr{L}_{m}) Gravity: A Comparative Analysis with Compact Objects
arxiv-2503-09222.creator: Sagar V. Soni, A. C. Khunt, Farook Rahaman, A. H. Hasmani
arxiv-2503-09222.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Sagar V. Soni, A. C. Khunt, Farook Rahaman, A. H. Hasmani. In this paper, we study the energy conditions of charged traversable wormholes in the framework of f ⁡ ( R , ℒ m ) f(R,\mathscr{L}_{m}) modified gravity. In the first case, we derive the shape functions (SFs) for two different choices of the charge function ℰ 2 \mathcal{E}^{2} by considering the Exponential Spheroid (ES) model and analyze the null energy condition (NEC).

arxiv-2509-03631.title: Lightweight image segmentation for echocardiography
arxiv-2509-03631.creator: Anders Kjelsrud 1 , Lasse Løvstakken 2 , Erik Smistad 2 3 , Håvard Dalen 2 4 , and Gilles Van De Vyver 2
arxiv-2509-03631.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Anders Kjelsrud 1 , Lasse Løvstakken 2 , Erik Smistad 2 3 , Håvard Dalen 2 4 , and Gilles Van De Vyver 2. Accurate segmentation of the left ventricle in echocardiography can enable fully automatic extraction of clinical measurements such as volumes and ejection fraction. While models configured by nnU-Net perform well, they are large and slow, thus limiting real-time use.

arxiv-2509-07792.title: Integer moments of the derivatives of the Riemann zeta function
arxiv-2509-07792.creator: Christopher Hughes, Andrew Pearce-Crump
arxiv-2509-07792.description: Abstract . We conjecture the full asymptotic expansion of a product of Riemann zeta functions, evaluated at the non-trivial zeros of the zeta function, with shifts added in each argument. By taking derivatives with respect to these shifts, we form a conjecture for the integer moments of mixed derivatives of the zeta function.

arxiv-2601-14492.title: UNCLE-Grasp: Uncertainty-Aware Grasping of Leaf-Occluded Strawberries
arxiv-2601-14492.creator: Malak Mansour, Ali Abouzeid, Zezhou Sun, Qinbo Sun, Dezhen Song, Abdalla Swikir
arxiv-2601-14492.description: Abstract Robotic strawberry harvesting is challenging under partial occlusion, where leaves induce significant geometric uncertainty and make grasp decisions based on a single deterministic shape estimate unreliable. From a single partial observation, multiple incompatible 3D completions may be plausible, causing grasps that appear feasible on one completion to fail on another.

arxiv-2602-16620.title: HOLISMOKES XX. Lens models of binary lens galaxies with five images of Supernova Winny
arxiv-2602-16620.creator: L. R. Ecker, A. G. Schweinfurth, R. Saglia, L. Deng, S. H. Suyu, C. Saulder, J. Snigula, R. Bender, R. Cañameras, T.-W. Chen, A. Galan, A. Halkola, E. Mamuzic, A. Melo, S. Schuldt, S. Taubenberger
arxiv-2602-16620.description: Abstract Strongly lensed supernovae (SNe) provide a powerful way to study cosmology, SNe and galaxies. Modelling the lens system is key to extracting astrophysical and cosmological information. We present adaptive-optics-assisted high-resolution images of the recently discovered SN Winny (SN 2025wny) in the J J and K K filters obtained with the Large Binocular Telescope.

pmc-10686968.title: High Rates of Undiagnosed Target Organ Damage Among Adults with Elevated Blood Pressure or Diabetes Mellitus in a Community-Based Survey in Lesotho
pmc-10686968.creator: Emmanuel Firima, Lucia Gonzalez, Moazziz Ali Khan, Molulela Manthabiseng, Mamoronts’sane P Sematle, Matumaole Bane, Makhebe Khomolishoele, Ikhetheleng Leisa, Lefokotsane Retselisitsoe, Thilo Burkard, Eleonara Seelig, Tristan Lee, Frédérique Chammartin, Ravi Gupta, Bailah Leigh, Maja Weisser, Alain A
pmc-10686968.description: IntroductionPrevalence of elevated blood pressure (BP) and diabetes mellitus (DM) is increasing in sub-Saharan Africa. Data on target organ damage such as retinopathy, left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), renal impairment and peripheral neuropathy (PN) among persons with elevated BP and/or DM in sub-Saharan Africa remain scarce.

pmc-10709544.title: Phosphate deficiency induced by infection promotes synthesis of anthracnose-resistant anthocyanin-3-O-galactoside phytoalexins in the Camellia sinensis plant
pmc-10709544.creator: Tongtong Li, Shenrong Wang, Dandan Shi, Wen Fang, Ting Jiang, Lixin Zhang, Yajun Liu, Liping Gao, Tao Xia
pmc-10709544.description: Tea (Camellia sinensis) is a well-known beverage crop rich in polyphenols with health benefits for humans. Understanding how tea polyphenols participate in plant resistance is beneficial to breeding resistant varieties and uncovering the resistance mechanisms. Here, we report that a Colletotrichum infection-induced ‘pink ring’ symptom appeared outside the lesion, which is highly likely to occur in resistant cultivars.

pmc-11377351.title: ‘Risk-benefit’ assessment for comprehensive safety evaluation of Chinese patent medicines containing four common toxic ingredients: an analysis of clinical risk factors
pmc-11377351.creator: Nan Zhang, Changming Zhong, Guoxiu Liu, Siyu Li, Li Lin, Namin Wei, Yu Song, Xiaoqing Wan, Yanping Wang, Yongyan Wang, Wanlin Wu, Zhongzhi Qian, Huaqiang Zhai
pmc-11377351.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundChinese patent medicines are specialty preparations in China that are produced using traditional prescriptions processed by modern pharmaceutical technology. They contain complex ingredients and much attention is paid to their clinical safety.

pmc-11462998.title: Ultra-processed foods and the incidence of pre-diabetes and type 2 diabetes among Iranian adults: the Tehran lipid and glucose study
pmc-11462998.creator: Nazanin Moslehi, Maryam Mahdavi, Parvin Mirmiran, Fereidoun Azizi
pmc-11462998.description: BackgroundNo study has investigated the association between ultra-processed food (UPF) and pre-diabetes development. Furthermore, prior investigations on the association between UPF and the risk of type 2 diabetes (T2D) were primarily conducted in Europe and America, and studies in other regions are lacking.

pmc-11542289.title: Clinical Significance of Combined Detection of CCL22 and IL‐1 as Potential New Bronchial Inflammatory Mediators in Children's Asthma
pmc-11542289.creator: Lei Cui, Xiaozhen Song, Yanping Peng, Min Shi
pmc-11542289.description: BackgroundsSevere asthma is a significant health burden because children with severe asthma are vulnerable to medication‐related side effects, life‐threatening deterioration, and impaired quality of life. However, there is a lack of data to elucidate the role of inflammatory variables in asthma.

pmc-11671992.title: CLinical EValuation of WEB 17 device in intracranial aneuRysms (CLEVER): procedural, 30-day and 1-year safety results for ruptured and unruptured aneurysms
pmc-11671992.creator: Laurent Spelle, Vincent Costalat, Jildaz Caroff, Fritz Wodarg, Sebastian Fischer, Denis Herbreteau, Markus A Möhlenbruch, Anne-Christine Januel, Chrysanthi Papagiannaki, Joachim Klisch, Jussi Numminen, Riitta Rautio, Ansgar Berlis, Cristian Mihalea, Vanessa Chalumeau, Jonathan Downer, Jonathan Corte
pmc-11671992.description: ABSTRACTBackgroundIntrasaccular flow disruption is an endovascular approach for the treatment of wide-neck aneurysms and, more specifically, wide-neck bifurcation aneurysms, which are challenging to treat with previously developed technologies. The Woven EndoBridge (WEB) device has demonstrated its efficacy and safety, for both unruptured and ruptured aneurysms.

pmc-11710709.title: Exploring the differential impact of sociodemographic and extrinsic factors on mobility‐based digital phenotypes versus standard cognitive tests among older adults
pmc-11710709.creator: Katherine Hackett, Shiyun Xu, Moira McKniff, Ian Barnett, Tania Giovannetti
pmc-11710709.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPassively‐obtained smartphone digital phenotypes may yield objective estimates of everyday cognition in older adults compared to traditional cognitive/self‐report measures typically confounded by sociodemographics. However, it is currently unknown what covariates are relevant when interpreting smartphone sensor data.

pmc-12449675.title: Leveraging Influencers to Reach and Engage Vulnerable Individuals With a Digital Health Intervention: Quasi-Experimental Field Study
pmc-12449675.creator: Marcia Nißen, Samira Harperink, Priyam Joshi, Anja Yvonne Bischof, Theresa Schachner, Yanick Xavier Lukic, Fabian Schneider, Prabhakaran Santhanam, Florian v Wangenheim, Joseph Ollier, Tobias Kowatsch
pmc-12449675.description: BackgroundNoncommunicable diseases are the leading cause of death, present economic challenges to health care systems worldwide, and disproportionally affect vulnerable individuals with low socioeconomic status (SES). While digital health interventions (DHIs) offer scalable and cost-effective solutions to promote health literacy and encourage behavior change, key challenges concern how to effectively reach and engage vulnerable individuals.

pmc-12557190.title: Close Space Sublimation Growth of Sb2(S,Se)3 Thin-Film Solar Cells
pmc-12557190.creator: Daniya A. Sindi, Thomas P. Shalvey, Matthew. J. Smiles, Tim. D. Veal, Leon Bowen, Jonathan. D. Major
pmc-12557190.description: This study reports the synthesis and characterization of Sb2(S,Se)3 thin films for thin-film photovoltaics via a single-source close space sublimation (CSS) approach. We demonstrate power conversion efficiencies of up to 4.3% with notable improvements in open-circuit voltage (V oc >490 mV) compared to those of Sb2Se3 equivalents.

pmc-13017710.title: Characterizing Treatment Adherence Trajectories in the endTB Multisite Cohort of Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis Patients: An Application of Group-Based Trajectory Modeling
pmc-13017710.creator: Stephanie Law, Isabel Fulcher, Samreen Ashraf, Mathieu Bastard, Wisny Docteur, Molly F Franke, Dalia Guerra, Catherine Hewison, Helena Huerga, Munira Khan, Palwasha Khan, Uzma Khan, Jarmila Kliescikova, Andargachew Kumsa, Nino Lomtadze, Fauziah Asnely Putri, Michael L Rich, Kwonjun Seung, Alena Skra
pmc-13017710.description: BackgroundIn tuberculosis (TB) care, adherence is often assessed using a simple 80% threshold, which may overlook meaningful patterns. We analyzed adherence trajectories among individuals treated for rifampicin- or multidrug-resistant TB (RR/MDR-TB) in the endTB observational study to identify more informative patterns.MethodsWe applied a joint latent class mixed model to classify adherence trajectories and assess their relationship with treatment outcomes.

pmc-13412779.title: Bictegravir/Tenofovir Alafenamide/Emtricitabine in Real-Life: A Multi-Year Experience
pmc-13412779.creator: Anna Gidari, Elena Baranello, Carlo Pallotto, Sabrina Morosi, Chiara Papalini, Giulia Gamboni, Lisa Malincarne, Daniele Rosignoli, Maria Carolina Benvenuto, Giacomo Gonnelli, Claudio Ucciferri, Giuseppe Vittorio De Socio
pmc-13412779.description: Introduction: Long-term real-world data on bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (BIC-STR), particularly in key subgroups, remain limited. The primary endpoints of the study were changes in CD4+ cell count and viral load after BIC-STR introduction. The secondary endpoints were the impact of the therapy on metabolic profile and body mass index.

pmc-13485421.title: Long-term Impact of COVID-19–Related Behavioral Changes on Myopia Progression in Children: A Four-Year Cohort Study
pmc-13485421.creator: Young Min Park, Hye Young Kim, Kwanghyun Lee
pmc-13485421.description: PurposeTo evaluate the effect of behavioral changes during the COVID-19 pandemic on myopia progression in children and to determine whether these changes modified the efficacy of low-concentration atropine.MethodsThis retrospective longitudinal study included children aged 7 to 15 years who underwent annual examinations from 2019 to 2023. A subset of participants completed a behavioral questionnaire in 2021.

pmc-13583657.title: Bicruciate-retaining versus cruciate-retaining total knee arthroplasty in implant fixation: a 10-year follow-up of a randomized RSA trial
pmc-13583657.creator: Tomofumi KINOSHITA, Kristian R L MORTENSEN, Lina H INGELSRUD, Omar MUHAREMOVIC, Kirill GROMOV, Anders TROELSEN
pmc-13583657.description: Background and purposeBicruciate-retaining (BCR) total knee arthroplasty (TKA) aims to restore physiological knee kinematics and joint stability by preserving both cruciate ligaments, potentially improving patient satisfaction. However, long-term clinical outcomes and tibial component migration remain insufficiently understood. We therefore aimed to evaluate long-term implant fixation and clinical outcome after BCR-TKA compared with cruciate-retaining (CR) TKA.

pmc-13599720.title: Risk Factors of Residual Exotropia After Surgery in Patients with Intermittent and Sensory Exotropia: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13599720.creator: Yara S Alhenaki, Mohammed A Alanazi, Amirah A Alanazi, Munira M Albeshr, Faeeqah Almhmoudi, Mohammed A Salawi, Hanan T Aljadani, Eyad M Albarrati, Nawaf I Almaiman
pmc-13599720.description: BackgroundResidual exotropia remains a common challenge following surgical correction of intermittent exotropia (IXT) and sensory exotropia (SX). Identifying prognostic factors associated with postoperative misalignment is essential to improve surgical planning and long-term outcomes.ObjectiveTo systematically review and evaluate patient- and surgery-related risk factors for residual exotropia after surgical correction, and to compare these factors between intermittent and sensory exotropia.

pmc-13602138.description: blished in Biological Psychiatry: Global Open Science, Liu et al.
